title: Integration of Explainability in Recommender Systems to Enhance Enterprise Value Strategies
tldr: Explores value-aware recommender systems (VARS) and explainable AI (XAI) integration to balance business value generation with recommendation transparency in enterprise contexts.
problem_and_motivation: Recommender systems are widely deployed in e-commerce, streaming, and advertising, but most focus on accuracy rather than business value. Companies need recommendations that optimize economic indicators like revenue, profit, and customer lifetime value. However, end-users must understand recommendations to achieve the best trade-off between demand and response, creating a need for explainable value-aware systems.
approach: Conducted the first systematic literature review on Value-Aware Recommender Systems (VARS) following PRISMA guidelines, analyzing 109 studies from IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM, and Springer.
Proposed a novel VARS taxonomy dividing algorithms into in-processing and post-processing approaches, further classified as value objective, value reinforcement, value ranking, and value policy.
Developed XVMF (Explainable Value-aware Matrix Factorization), a novel model balancing recommendation profit and explainability using regularization terms.
Surveyed graph-based explainable recommender systems (GxRS) and identified the lack of standardized evaluation methods for explanation quality in graph-based models.
Evaluated XVMF on Yelp and Amazon datasets comparing against standard MF and EMF baselines using accuracy, ranking, and explanation quality metrics.
Designed an extension of Matrix Factorization that incorporates item value information and produces explainable recommendations simultaneously.
Formulated the trade-off between value optimization and explainability as a multi-objective problem controlled by regularization parameters.
findings: num: PRISMA review identified 109 VARS studies from 45,614 initial records, with 4 main technical categories identified in the proposed taxonomy.
num: VARS algorithms are predominantly applied in product recommendation (most frequent), advertising, news, and media recommendation domains.
num: In-processing algorithms (value objective, value reinforcement) modify model objectives to directly optimize value, while post-processing algorithms rerank existing recommendations.
num: Reinforcement learning approaches in VARS define reward functions based on business value metrics like customer lifetime value and click-conversion rate.
num: Graph-based explainable recommender systems lack standardized evaluation frameworks for explanation quality, hindering comparability.
num: XVMF model on Yelp dataset showed that increasing explainability regularization reduces ranking quality (NDCG) but improves explanation metrics (E-NDCG).
num: The trade-off between business value and explainability can be systematically controlled via regularization parameters in matrix factorization.
num: Post-processing value ranking approaches use weighted interest formulas (r_hat * v_i) to balance accuracy with profitability.
num: Dynamic pricing integration in VARS enables personalized price optimization based on customer willingness to pay.
num: Knowledge Graphs and GNNs show promise for explainable recommendations but explanation evaluation remains insufficiently rigorous.

key_equations.explanation: Standard recommendation objective: maximize expected user interest by selecting top-k items with highest predicted scores.

key_equations.equation: argmax_{Y_{u,k}} sum_{i in Y_{u,k}} r_hat_{u,i} * v_i
key_equations.explanation: Value ranking objective: incorporates item value v_i to balance user interest with business value.

key_equations.equation: argmax_{Y_{u,k}} sum_{i in Y_{u,k}} (1 - alpha) * r_hat_{u,i} + alpha * v_i
key_equations.explanation: Trade-off objective: regularization parameter alpha controls balance between accuracy and profitability.
Matrix factorization prediction: dot product of user latent vector p_u and item latent vector q_i.

key_equations.equation: max E[Omega(tau)], Omega(tau) = sum_{t=0}^{tau} gamma^t * omega(a_t, s_t)
key_equations.explanation: Reinforcement learning objective: maximize expected discounted cumulative reward where reward incorporates item value.

definitions.definition: Recommender systems designed to directly maximize one or more business indicators (e.g., revenue, profit, CTR) to achieve business objectives.
AI methods that promote transparency in recommender systems by providing understandable explanations for recommendations to users.
A novel recommender model proposed in this thesis that balances business profit generation with explainability features through regularization.
VARS methods applied after any base recommendation algorithm to re-rank outputs based on economic value without modifying the original model.
VARS methods that modify the objective function or architecture of the recommendation algorithm itself to directly optimize business value.

topics.name: Machine Learning Algorithms
topics.justification: Thesis proposes XVMF, a novel matrix factorization algorithm, and surveys ML-based recommender algorithms including RL, GNN, and KG methods.

topics.name: Financial Technology
topics.justification: Focuses on business value generation through recommender systems for enterprise applications including e-commerce and advertising.

topics.name: Explainable AI
topics.justification: Core contribution is integrating explainability (XAI) into recommender systems; includes taxonomy of explanation styles and evaluation methods.

topics.name: Systematic Reviews & Surveys
topics.justification: Contains a PRISMA-based systematic literature review of VARS with 109 included studies and a taxonomy of value-aware algorithms.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides the first PRISMA-based systematic literature review of Value-Aware Recommender Systems with a novel technical taxonomy, proposes XVMF as a model balancing business value and explainability, and identifies critical gaps in evaluation of graph-based explainable recommender systems.
directly_justifies: Selection of ML algorithms (matrix factorization, RL, GNN) for value-aware and explainable recommendation in Odin's budget management features.
Framework for evaluating trade-offs between predictive accuracy and business value in recommender systems.
limits: Thesis primarily focuses on e-commerce and media domains rather than personal finance management.
VARS taxonomy does not extensively cover budget management or personal financial planning applications.
Only available as a Ph.D. thesis which may limit accessibility.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Primary topics 4.B (ML algorithms for recommendation), 7.B (fintech value generation), 8.A (explainable AI), and 12.A (systematic review methodology).

limitations: PRISMA review limited to four databases (IEEE, Scopus, ACM, Springer) and English-language peer-reviewed articles only.
Graduate theses and doctoral dissertations were excluded from the systematic review.
VARS research predominantly focuses on product recommendation; personal finance applications remain underexplored.
Graph-based explainable recommender evaluation lacks standardized quantitative benchmarks.
XVMF model tested only on two datasets (Yelp, Amazon) limiting generalizability.
remember_this: First PRISMA systematic review of Value-Aware Recommender Systems with 109 studies.
XVMF balances business value and explainability via regularization in matrix factorization.
Graph-based explainable RS lack standardized evaluation frameworks for explanation quality.
Reinforcement learning enables long-term value optimization in recommendation through reward design.
Post-processing reranking can inject value awareness into any existing recommender system.
